turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I’m pretty sure the people at my apartment are watching when I come and go. They’re slipping notes about me to the office, and everybody keeps saying it’s just regular notices on the doors, but that’s not how it feels to me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a belief that apartment residents are monitoring their movements and secretly submitting notes about them despite others offering a benign explanation.

Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I hear noises in the building sometimes, but not voices talking to me when nobody’s there.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient denies hearing voices when nobody is present, while distinguishing this from nonspecific building noises.

turns.doctor_question: When did you first start feeling that the people at your apartment were watching you?
turns.patient_response: It started a little over a year ago... maybe about a year and a month. That’s when I really started feeling like the neighbors and the office were keeping track of me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reports a belief that neighbors and people at the office were keeping track of them, beginning about a year and a month ago.

turns.doctor_question: During this time, have you had a period when you felt unusually depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already gone bad before I even get out of bed. It’s there a lot of the day.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient endorses a heavy, hollow depressed feeling on most mornings that persists for much of the day.

turns.doctor_question: Have you found yourself losing interest or motivation to do the things you used to do?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I have. I used to look forward to choir practice, playing bridge, cooking beans on Sundays… even doing little repair jobs for people. Now I mostly just let the phone ring and tell myself there’s no point in going.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient reports no longer looking forward to several previously enjoyed activities and withdrawing from invitations, indicating loss of interest and motivation.

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when you still felt watched even when you were not feeling depressed?
turns.patient_response: Yes. There was a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling quite as low—I was eating a little better and not waking up so hopeless. But even then, I still felt like the neighbors were watching my door and telling somebody about me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: During several weeks of improved depressive symptoms, the patient still believed neighbors were watching her door and reporting on her, indicating a persecutory belief.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever believed that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside of you?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know about thoughts being put in my mind exactly. What I do know is I came in because I’m sure the people at my apartment are watching when I come and go, and they’re slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody says they’re just regular notices on the doors, but that’s not how it feels to me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed-seeming belief that apartment residents are monitoring their comings and goings and sending notes about them despite others offering a benign explanation.

turns.doctor_question: Have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I guess I don’t talk as much as I used to, but I haven’t been paying close attention to it. Some days I just don’t feel like saying much.

turns.doctor_question: Has there been a time when you felt watched like this for at least two weeks while you were not feeling depressed?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It went on for several weeks. I wasn’t feeling as depressed then—I was eating a little better and not waking up feeling so hopeless—but I still thought the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reports believing that neighbors were watching their door and reporting on them for several weeks, consistent with a persecutory delusional belief.

turns.doctor_question: Have you found yourself showing much less emotion on your face or in your voice than you used to?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my face or voice being different like that. I mean, I might seem flat sometimes when I’m tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than before.

turns.doctor_question: Has a doctor ever told you that you have a brain or nervous system illness, like epilepsy, a head injury, or dementia?
turns.patient_response: Not that I know of. No doctor has told me I have something like epilepsy or dementia or a brain injury.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I can’t really remember a time where I felt unusually high or euphoric like that.

turns.doctor_question: Have these beliefs that your neighbors are watching you been present for at least one month?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s been longer than a month. I’d say those thoughts about the neighbors and the office have been going on for about a year… maybe a year and a month.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms persistent suspicious beliefs that neighbors and people at the office are watching them, present for about a year and a month.

turns.doctor_question: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?
turns.patient_response: Yes, some people have said that. When I’m trying to explain something, I’ll start talking about the rent, then I’m on to the marina, then the choir robes, and the wires in the walls… and people look at me like I skipped over half the story. I don’t always notice it until I see their face.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient reports that others say their explanations are hard to follow and describes jumping among unrelated topics in a way that leaves listeners confused.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really seen things that other people couldn’t see, not that I can remember.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient states they have not seen things that other people could not see, denying visual hallucinations.

turns.doctor_question: During the past year that these beliefs about your neighbors have been going on, have you felt depressed for most of that time?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Most of that time since I moved, I’ve felt pretty low. Even on days where I could talk a little clearer or seem okay, underneath I still felt useless and didn’t really care about doing the things I used to like.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient states that for most of the time since moving they have felt "pretty low."
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient says they did not really care about doing things they used to like, indicating diminished interest or pleasure.
symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient reports feeling useless, consistent with feelings of worthlessness.
